name: CONSORT 2010
source: Schulz KF, Altman DG, Moher D, for the CONSORT Group. CONSORT 2010 Statement: updated guidelines for reporting parallel group randomised trials. BMJ. 2010;340:c332 / PLoS Med. 2010;7(3):e1000251. https://www.consort-statement.org/ | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2844794/ | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2844940/

items.text: Identify the study as a randomized trial in the title.
Provide a structured abstract summarizing trial design, methods, results, and conclusions.
Explain the scientific background and rationale for conducting the trial.
State the specific objectives or hypotheses tested by the trial.
Describe the trial design, such as parallel or factorial, and the allocation ratio.
Report any major changes to methods after trial start and explain why.
Specify participant eligibility criteria.
Describe the settings and locations where trial data were collected.
Detail each group's intervention, including how and when it was delivered, to allow replication.
Define all pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes, including how and when they were measured.
Report any changes to trial outcomes after the trial began, with reasons.
Explain how the target sample size was calculated.
Describe any interim analyses and stopping rules, if applicable.
Describe the method used to generate the random allocation sequence.
Specify the randomization type and any restrictions such as blocking and block sizes.
Describe how the allocation sequence was implemented and concealed until group assignment.
State who generated the sequence, enrolled participants, and assigned them to interventions.
State who was blinded after assignment and how blinding was maintained.
Describe the physical similarity of compared interventions, if relevant.
Specify statistical methods used to compare groups for primary and secondary outcomes.
Specify statistical methods for additional analyses such as subgroup or adjusted analyses.
Report per group the numbers randomized, receiving intended treatment, and analyzed for the primary outcome.
Report losses and exclusions after randomization for each group, with reasons.
State the calendar dates defining recruitment and follow-up periods.
Explain why the trial ended or was stopped early.
Present a table of baseline demographic and clinical characteristics for each group.
Report participant denominators in each analysis per group and whether analysis followed original assignment.
Present group results, estimated effect size, and precision for every primary and secondary outcome.
Present both absolute and relative effect sizes for binary outcomes.
Report results of subgroup and adjusted analyses, distinguishing pre-specified from exploratory ones.
Report all important adverse events or unintended effects observed in each group.
Discuss trial limitations, including sources of bias, imprecision, and multiplicity of analyses.
Discuss external validity and applicability of the trial results.
Interpret findings consistently with results, balancing benefits and harms against other evidence.
Provide the trial registration number and name of the registry.
State where the full trial protocol can be accessed, if available.
State funding and support sources, such as drug supply, and the role of funders.
